body:
"On the World Wide Web, Foster found
 both the Unabomber manifesto and a 1971 Kaczynski essay..."

That would be the copy we scanned on the "Truth Is Redacted" page ... (it was
the only copy on the web).


[Foster notes] a preference for the "corrected" cliche: "You can't eat your
cake and have it, too." Soon requests
 for Foster's forensic skills came pouring in."

Hey, wait a minute.  Tehehe.  Foster got this from our newsgroup.  Erik,
remember?  I posted four citations showing that it was the correct cliche in
response to a secret post by a young
woman from the federal defender's office
(who had seen the internet posts on the subject but was looking for authority).
 (I knew Karen O. was from the Federal Defender's office because she had a
revealing com name in a post in which she tried to sell her sister's Olympic
tickets.)  Foster should split his fee with us.  
*************
This is the post from the Federal Defender's office in this newsgroup when they
were looking for authority --

	"I have heard that the Unabomber's use [of the phrase ï¿½you canï¿½t eat your cake
and eat it tooï¿½] was the original arrangement of this phrase which was started
sometime in the 1500's.  The logic being that you can eat your cake and once
eaten, it is not reasonable to expect to still have possession of it. ...  I
understand that the phrase got turned around in the 1940's.  Can anyone confirm
this information?
		Karen Oglesby
		in alt.fan.unabomber"

Karen O. was the computer person in the office.
